html:
Ahmad al-Mansur was the Saadi sultan of Morocco from 1578 to 1603, who came to the throne after the Battle of the Three Kings and made Morocco a power respected in Europe.

With ransom money and sugar profits he built the great El Badi palace in Marrakesh. In 1591 he sent an army with guns across the Sahara, which defeated the Songhai Empire at the Battle of Tondibi and took Timbuktu and Gao. Gold and slaves flowed north for a time, earning him the name al-Dhahabi, the golden.

He wrote to Elizabeth I of England about an alliance against Spain. After his death in 1603 his sons fought over the throne and the Saadi state broke apart.
sum: Ahmad al-Mansur was the Saadi sultan of Morocco from 1578 to 1603, who came to the throne after the Battle of the Three Kings and made Morocco a power respected in Europe.
